# Real, simulated, and not tested

Nothing in the F2 proof of concept is a production system.

The architecture mechanics are real: processes, protocols, persistence, signals, retries and traces. The enterprise behind them is simulated.

## Real

| What | How it is real | Where |
|---|---|---|
| MCP protocol | Official Python SDK `mcp==2.2.0` servers and clients, over stdio, in separate OS processes | `mcp_servers/servers.py`, `layered_platform/tools/mcp_client.py`, `monolith/incident_agent.py` |
| Model calls | Local Ollama: `gpt-oss:20b` (model A) and `qwen3:8b` (model B), temperature 0, fixed seeds | `layered_platform/models/ollama.py`, `monolith/incident_agent.py` |
| Durable state | SQLite in WAL mode with `synchronous=FULL`; append-only checkpoints written in one transaction | `layered_platform/runtime/checkpoints.py` |
| Process termination | `os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGKILL)` at a named point. There are no `finally` blocks and no flush; the harness sees exit code −9 | `crashpoints.py`, `experiments/runners/harness.py` |
| Restart | A new OS process picks the work up: `recover()` in the layered platform, a re-submitted request in the monolith | `experiments/runners/scenario.py` |
| Timeouts and retries | Real client-side MCP read timeouts; real retries | `tools/gateway.py`, `monolith/incident_agent.py` |
| Idempotency | A deterministic op id is sent as the backend key; the backend stores and replays the result | `tools/idempotency.py`, `simulated_enterprise/world.py` |
| Policy and approvals | Evaluated in code from YAML rules; approvals are bound by digest to one action | `layered_platform/policy/` |
| Tracing | OpenTelemetry SDK spans, exported to fsynced JSONL and continued across processes | `layered_platform/telemetry/tracing.py` |
| Tests | pytest, run inside the recorded run; results are in `runs/<id>/tests.json` | `tests/` |
| Record/replay | Every model call is taped at the HTTP boundary. Replay serves the tape and re-executes everything else | `recordreplay/tape.py`, `scripts/replay_run.py` |
| Change diffs | Real `git diff` of committed patches in throwaway worktrees | `experiments/runners/harness.py` |

## Simulated

| What | Simulation | Consequence for the claims |
|---|---|---|
| Incident management (ITSM) | A JSON document in SQLite | Ticket semantics are simplified |
| Deployment backend | `rollback_release` rewrites a "running release" row and advances a simulated clock. `deploy_v2` is the same world behind a different interface | A rollback is instantaneous and always succeeds |
| Observability | Metric shapes and log lines from `inc4917.yaml`; they recover 3 simulated minutes after a rollback to a healthy release | Verification cannot fail for reasons outside the scenario |
| Backend idempotency | Implemented by the simulator: a same key with the same arguments replays, a same key with different arguments is refused | The E4 and E5 results depend on a backend that honours keys. Many do; not all |
| Identity | `config/principals.yaml`: `sre.alice` (responder) and `ic.bob` (incident commander) | There is no authentication, only role lookup |
| Approver | `ic.bob` approves every request it is shown, in both architectures | This measures where approval happens, not human judgement |
| Faults | Armed in the world database and applied inside the MCP server: a lost response is a committed write, then an 8 s silence against a 5 s client timeout | One fault shape per experiment |
| Production infrastructure | None. One laptop, one process per phase, local models | Latency and token counts are properties of this machine and these models |
| `flush_sessions` | A write tool present on the deploy server that neither agent's author listed | A constructed but common situation: servers add tools after agents are written |

## Not tested

- More than one scenario (INC-4917 only).
- Concurrency: several workflows, several workers, or contention on a lease.
- Multi-host failure (leases use pid liveness on one host).
- A provider change with a different wire API (both models are served by Ollama).
- Real human approval latency and judgement.
- Network partitions other than the lost-response fault.
- Throughput or scale.
- Any claim of exactly-once delivery. The guarantee shown is effectively-once execution when the backend honours the key.
